q: Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on equity-oriented mutual funds (held > 12 months) above ₹1.25 lakh are taxed at:
e: Post Budget 2024 (effective 23 July 2024), LTCG on equity above ₹1.25 lakh exemption is taxed at 12.5% (without indexation).

q: Short Term Capital Gains (STCG) on equity-oriented mutual funds (held ≤ 12 months) are taxed at:
e: Post Budget 2024, STCG on equity is taxed at 20% (raised from 15%).

q: For debt mutual funds purchased on or after 1 April 2023, gains are:
o: Treated as STCG and taxed at applicable slab rate, regardless of holding period
e: From 1 April 2023, debt fund gains are added to income and taxed at slab rate — indexation benefit removed for new investments.

q: For an equity-oriented hybrid fund (≥65% equity), taxation follows:
e: Equity-oriented hybrids (≥65% equity) follow equity taxation: STCG 20%, LTCG 12.5% above ₹1.25L.

q: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is applicable on:
e: STT applies to redemption/switch out of equity-oriented schemes. Not on debt funds.

q: Dividends from mutual funds are taxable in the hands of:
e: Post April 2020, dividends (now called IDCW) are taxable in investor hands at slab rate. DDT regime abolished.

q: For ELSS, the tax deduction under Section 80C is up to:
e: ELSS qualifies for deduction up to ₹1.5 lakh under Section 80C (old tax regime only — not in new regime).

q: TDS on capital gains from mutual funds applies to:
e: TDS applies on capital gains for NRIs (rates vary by holding period and scheme type). Not deducted for resident individuals.

q: Indexation benefit currently applies to:
e: Indexation now applies only to debt funds purchased BEFORE 1 April 2023, when held long-term. New debt purchases get no indexation.

q: A switch between two schemes of the same AMC is:
o: A taxable event — capital gain/loss is computed
e: Switch is treated as redemption + fresh purchase — a taxable event. Holding period of original units determines STCG/LTCG.

q: Holding period for LONG-term classification of debt fund units (purchased before April 2023) is:
e: For debt funds (pre-April 2023 purchases), >36 months holding qualifies as long-term. For equity, the threshold is >12 months.

q: Capital loss from equity mutual funds can be:
o: Set off only against equity gains, carried forward 8 years
e: STCL can be set off against any capital gain. LTCL only against LTCG. Both can be carried forward 8 assessment years.

q: LTCG on equity-oriented MFs above ₹1.25L is taxed at:
e: 12.5% post Budget 2024.

q: STCG on equity-oriented MFs is taxed at:
e: 20% post Budget 2024.

q: Debt funds purchased post-April 2023 are taxed at:
e: Slab rate — no indexation for new purchases.

q: Switch from one MF scheme to another is:
e: Taxable event — capital gain/loss computed.

q: STT applies on:
e: Equity-oriented scheme redemptions.

q: For tax purposes, an Arbitrage Fund is generally treated as:
e: Arbitrage funds maintain ≥65% gross equity exposure (cash + futures) and are taxed as equity-oriented schemes.

q: STT (Securities Transaction Tax) is applicable on:
o: Redemption / switch out of equity-oriented MF schemes
e: STT applies to redemption and switch-out of equity-oriented schemes. Not levied on debt fund transactions.

q: Section 80C deduction for ELSS investment is available only under the:
e: Sec 80C deduction (up to ₹1.5 lakh) for ELSS is available only under the OLD tax regime. The new regime does not permit most deductions.

q: For an investor in the highest tax bracket, the most tax-efficient form of mutual fund earning is generally:
o: Growth option held >12 months for equity LTCG
e: Growth + LTCG (12.5% above ₹1.25L for equity) is typically more tax-efficient than IDCW (taxed at slab rate). Less frequent transactions also reduce STT/STCG drag.

q: Stamp duty on mutual fund unit issuance/transfer was introduced from:
e: Stamp duty on mutual fund units (issuance and transfer) was introduced from 1 July 2020 — 0.005% on issuance and 0.015% on transfer.

q: The rate of stamp duty applicable to mutual fund unit issuance is:
e: Stamp duty on issuance (purchase / SIP / dividend reinvestment) is 0.005% of the transaction value.

q: A Fund of Funds (FoF) investing in equity-oriented schemes is taxed as per:
e: Until recently, ALL FoFs were taxed as debt (slab rate). Post Budget 2024, FoFs that hold ≥65% in equity-oriented MF units may qualify for equity tax — verify the latest rule for the specific FoF.

q: Equity-oriented schemes are taxed favourably only if they invest a minimum of __ in domestic equities.
e: For favourable equity taxation (LTCG @ 12.5%, STCG @ 20%), the scheme must hold ≥65% in domestic equities, calculated on a quarterly average basis.

q: For LTCG on equity-oriented mutual funds, the exemption threshold is:
e: Post Budget 2024 (effective 23 July 2024), LTCG exemption is ₹1.25 lakh per financial year (raised from ₹1 lakh).

q: For an investor in a higher tax bracket, dividends from mutual funds (IDCW) are:
o: Taxed at slab rate in investor hands
e: IDCW (dividends) are taxable at slab rate in investor hands (post April 2020). DDT regime is abolished.

q: For a debt fund purchased BEFORE 1 April 2023 and held >36 months, the holder gets:
e: Pre-April 2023 debt fund purchases held >36 months still qualify for LTCG @ 20% with indexation. Post-April 2023 purchases are slab-taxed.

q: Income earned by a mutual fund scheme is:
o: Taxed as per the marginal tax rate of investors
Exempt from tax under Section 10(23D) of Income Tax Act
e: Section 10(23D) of Income Tax Act exempts all income earned by mutual fund schemes from tax. Tax incidence falls on the unitholder.

q: Redemption from which fund attracts STT (Securities Transaction Tax) for an investor?
e: STT applies on redemption of equity-oriented schemes (≥65% equity). Multi-cap is equity-oriented. Debt funds (G-Sec, Liquid, Overnight) attract no STT.

q: An investor in 30% tax slab earns ₹10,000 IDCW. After-tax dividend is:
e: IDCW is taxed at slab rate. ₹10,000 × (1 − 0.30) = ₹7,000. (Plus surcharge/cess applicable.)

q: LTCG of ₹2,50,000 on equity-oriented scheme units. Tax payable (at 12.5% post Budget 2024, ₹1.25L exemption):
STCG of ₹50,000 on equity scheme. Tax payable (at 20% post Budget 2024):
For an investor in 30% tax slab, redeems ₹50,000 STCG from a debt fund (purchased post-April 2023). Tax payable:
e: Post-April 2023 debt fund gains are taxed at slab rate regardless of holding period. 30% slab × ₹50,000 = ₹15,000.

q: An investor has STCL of ₹30,000 from equity. Can be set off against:
o: Any capital gain (both LTCG and STCG, equity or debt)
e: Short-Term Capital Loss can be set off against ANY capital gain (long-term or short-term, equity or debt). Long-Term Capital Loss can only be set off against LTCG.

q: An equity-oriented FoF that invests in domestic equity-oriented schemes — for taxation, it is treated as:
e: Post Budget 2024 update: Equity-oriented FoFs that invest ≥90% in equity-oriented schemes can be taxed as equity (12.5% LTCG above ₹1.25L). Verify per latest rules.

q: For ELSS investments via SIP, the 3-year lock-in applies:
o: Once for the entire SIP from first installment
Separately to EACH SIP installment from its date of investment
e: EACH SIP installment in ELSS is locked-in separately for 3 years from its own investment date. So a 12-month SIP's last installment is locked till 3 years after the 12th month.

q: Section 80C deduction for ELSS investment is available:
o: In both old and new tax regimes
Only in the OLD tax regime
Only in the new tax regime
e: Sec 80C (₹1.5L deduction) for ELSS is available ONLY in the OLD tax regime. The NEW regime offers lower slab rates but no most deductions.

q: Long-Term Capital Loss (LTCL) on equity-oriented MF can be set off against:
o: Only LTCG (long-term capital gains) from any source
e: LTCL can be set off ONLY against LTCG (any source). It cannot be set off against STCG, salary, or other income. Carry-forward allowed for 8 assessment years.

q: Short-Term Capital Loss (STCL) can be set off against:
o: Any capital gain (both STCG and LTCG, equity or debt)
e: STCL is more flexible — can be set off against ANY capital gain (LTCG or STCG, equity or debt). Carry-forward for 8 assessment years.

q: For an NRI redeeming an equity-oriented scheme (held >12 months) above ₹1.25L exemption, TDS rate is:
e: Post Budget 2024: TDS for NRIs on LTCG from equity-oriented schemes is 12.5% on amount above ₹1.25L exemption. Different from resident treatment.

q: For an NRI redeeming an equity-oriented scheme (held ≤12 months), TDS rate is:
e: Post Budget 2024: TDS for NRIs on STCG from equity-oriented schemes is 20%, matching the new STCG rate.

q: Stamp duty on mutual fund unit issuance is levied at:
e: Stamp duty on unit issuance: 0.005% (effective 1 July 2020). Applies to lump-sum, SIP, STP, switch-in, dividend reinvestment.

q: Stamp duty on transfer of mutual fund units (off-market) is levied at:
e: Off-market transfer of MF units (e.g., gifting): stamp duty 0.015%. Higher than issuance rate.

q: Bonus units allotted by a mutual fund have a cost of acquisition for tax purposes of:
o: NAV on the day of bonus
e: For tax computation, bonus units have ZERO cost of acquisition. When sold, the entire sale value is capital gain. Holding period reckoned from bonus issue date.

q: Indexation benefit (currently) is available for:
o: Debt fund LTCG ONLY for purchases made BEFORE 1 April 2023
e: Indexation now applies only to debt fund units PURCHASED before 1 April 2023, when held long-term. Post-April 2023 debt purchases are slab-rate taxed without indexation.

q: A switch from a regular plan to a direct plan within the same scheme is:
o: A taxable event — capital gain/loss must be computed
Free of any tax for first switch
e: Plan switch (regular → direct) is treated as redemption + fresh subscription. Capital gain/loss is computed. Holding period for original units determines tax treatment.

q: For STT on equity-oriented MF redemption — STT is paid by:
e: STT is borne by the investor — deducted from redemption proceeds. Rate is small but applies on equity-oriented scheme redemption/switch-out.

q: For ELSS investments via SIP, lock-in is computed:
o: From the first SIP installment for all units
Separately for EACH SIP installment from its own date
e: Each ELSS SIP installment locks separately for 3 years from its individual investment date.

q: For a non-resident Indian (NRI) selling equity-oriented MF units held >12 months — TDS rate (post Budget 2024) on amount above ₹1.25L:
e: NRI LTCG TDS on equity-oriented MF: 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25L. Matches resident LTCG rate post Budget 2024.

q: Bonus units in a mutual fund scheme have a cost of acquisition for tax of:
e: Bonus units: zero cost of acquisition. When sold, entire sale value is capital gain. Holding period reckoned from bonus issue date.

q: For a scheme to qualify as Equity-Oriented for tax — minimum equity exposure (computed on quarterly average basis):
e: Equity-oriented for tax: ≥65% in DOMESTIC equities (quarterly average). International funds investing in foreign equity don't qualify, despite holding equity.

q: An International Equity Fund (investing in foreign equity) is taxed as:
o: As per debt/non-equity rules — slab rate or specific (since it lacks 65% domestic equity)
e: Domestic-equity threshold (≥65%) is for the favourable equity tax. International funds fail this and are taxed under non-equity rules — typically slab rate post-April 2023.

q: For a Conservative Hybrid Fund (10-25% equity) — the equity portion is taxed:
o: As debt / non-equity (since equity <65%) — slab rate
e: Conservative Hybrid: equity is only 10-25%, fails the 65% threshold. Whole scheme taxed as debt/non-equity. Slab rate applies (post April 2023 purchases).

q: LTCG on equity-oriented schemes (held >12 months, post Budget 2024):
e: Post Budget 2024 (effective 23 July 2024): LTCG on equity above ₹1.25L is taxed at 12.5%. Below threshold is tax-free.

q: For a scheme to qualify as equity-oriented for taxation, equity allocation must be:
e: Equity-oriented for tax: ≥65% in DOMESTIC equities, on a quarterly average basis. Foreign equity does not count.

q: STT (Securities Transaction Tax) on equity-oriented MF redemption is:
o: Deducted from redemption proceeds (borne by investor)
e: STT is borne by the investor — deducted from redemption proceeds. Applies on equity-oriented scheme redemption/switch-out.

q: A "Fund of Funds" investing primarily (≥90%) in domestic equity-oriented schemes is taxed (post Budget 2024):
o: Can qualify as equity-oriented (12.5% LTCG above ₹1.25L)
e: Post Budget 2024: FoF investing ≥90% in domestic equity-oriented MF schemes can qualify for equity tax treatment. Other FoFs taxed as debt.
